name: Topics API (retired)
plain: Chrome's interest-topic API for ads. Deprecated in Chrome 144 and being removed in 2026.
meaning: Gave ad scripts up to 3 coarse interest topics (one per recent week) from the browsing history of sites that called it. Taxonomy had 469 topics in v2; 5% of results were random noise. Removal rolling out from Chrome 153.

access.persistence: Epoch of 1 week; 3 most recent epochs returned; observed topics kept for 3 weeks
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can't pick your interests from your browsing any more; Chrome is retiring this
limits.user_action: Nothing. It used to run when an ad script loaded in Chrome
can: Still work in some older Chrome versions until removal rolls out from Chrome 153
Hand ad scripts up to 3 broad interest topics, one per recent week
cannot: Run in Safari, Firefox, or Edge
Give exact sites you visited; it shared broad topics only, and 5% were random noise
Keep working after Chrome finishes removing it
Pick topics from sites that never used the feature
limits.differs: Only Chrome ever offered it. Other browsers never did.

story.what_it_is: Chrome's retired feature that told ad scripts a few broad interests, like Sports or Travel.

marketing.name: Topics API
marketing.pitch: Chrome described it as a way to show relevant ads using broad topics instead of tracking you across sites.

story.for_you: You may have seen an Ad topics switch in Chrome settings. Chrome noted a few broad interests from the sites you visit and shared them with ad scripts. This was being removed in 2026, so most people will never meet it.
story.for_makers: Ad companies wanted a replacement for cookies that still let them pick a relevant ad. Topics gave a coarse interest label with no name or ID attached. Few buyers adopted it, which is part of why it was dropped.

use_cases.example: An ad tech script on a news page asks Chrome for your topics and picks a travel ad because Travel was on the list.
A retailer's ad partner favours camping gear ads for visitors whose topics include Outdoors.
A browser games site shows a sports game promo to visitors whose topics include Fitness, without knowing who they are.
A publisher with many logged-out readers lifts ad income by sending topics along with the ad request.
An ad measurement firm compared topic-based ad results with cookie-based results during Chrome's trials.
Ad tech engineers ran Chrome origin trials and tuned their bidding code to use topic labels.

risks: Retired, so old code may linger

technical_bounds: Only returns topics the caller observed on prior sites
Up to 3 topics per call, 1 per epoch
Blocked when third-party cookies are off or user disabled Ad topics
Not shipped in Firefox or Safari; Edge disabled it

abuse: Profiling topics across sites by many callers

history.change: Topics shipped with Privacy Sandbox general availability
Oct 17 2025: Google announces retirement of Topics
Removal rollout: 1% stable on 153 and later, paused at 10% until Oct 15 2026, full removal after (per blink-dev as summarised Oct 2 2026)
